passages.text: ### 4.5 A fixed-time inequality and its plateau application **Proposition 4.1 (coercivity at a fixed time).** Let $\gamma\in\mathcal U$ and let $X$ be its associated diffusion, started at zero. Suppose that $00$. With $a=\Phi_{xx}$, $b=\Phi_{xxx}$ and $d=\Phi_{xxxx}$, evaluated at $(t,X_t)$, one has $$ \mathcal C_\gamma(t):=\mathbb E[d^2-12cab^2+6c^2a^4] \ge \frac{c^2}{1000}\mathbb E a^4. \tag{4.1} $$ Neither minimality nor a constant neighbourhood of $t$ is assumed. This is the common estimate behind plateau curvature and positive density. When $\gamma$ is smooth near $t$, Itô's formula gives $q''=\mathbb E b^2-2\gamma\mathbb E a^3$ and $$ (\mathbb E b^2)'=\mathbb E d^2-6\gamma\mathbb E(ab^2),\qquad (\mathbb E a^3)'=3\mathbb E(ab^2)-3\gamma\mathbb E a^4. $$ Differentiating the first identity therefore gives $$ q'''(t)+2\gamma'(t)\mathbb E a^3=\mathcal C_\gamma(t). \tag{4.2} $$ On a plateau the coefficient derivative vanishes. At a smooth minimizer, $q=t$ makes the third derivative of $q$ vanish instead. **Proof.** Fix $t **The spatial inequality at a coefficient jump.** Continuity at $t$ is a sufficient hypothesis in Proposition 4.1 and in the retained sampled formal interface. The ordinary spatial-moment argument permits a little more. Fix $c=\gamma(t)>0$ and replace $\gamma$ by $c$ on $[t-\delta,t+\delta)$, leaving it unchanged elsewhere. Monotonicity preserves both joins and right continuity. For fixed $0<\delta_0<\min(t,1-t)$ and $0<\delta\le\delta_0$, $$ \|\gamma_\delta-\gamma\|_1 \le2\delta\,\gamma(t+\delta_0)\longrightarrow0. $$ Thus local boundedness suffices for the same strip stability and coupled expectation limit. Each replacement has a positive plateau at $t$, so (4.1) holds at a jump too, with the stated right-continuous value $c$. This extension concerns spatial moments only: it supplies no time derivative $q'''(t)$ or $\gamma'(t)$ at a jump and does not remove a hypothesis from the retained Lean declaration. Neither application below requires this extension. **Corollary 4.2 (positive plateaus).** Suppose now that $\gamma=c>0$ on an open interval $I\subset(0,1)$ and $t\in I$. Then (4.2) gives $q'''(t)=\mathcal C_\gamma(t)$. To establish strictness for this limiting solution, choose $b\in I$ later than $t$ and put $\psi=\Phi_\gamma(b,\cdot)$. This is smooth, convex, even and a bounded distance from $|x|$, so $\psi'$ cannot be constant. The Cole–Hopf formula gives $$ \Phi_{xx}(t,x) =\mathbb E^{\rm tilt}_{t,x}\psi'' +c\operatorname{Var}^{\rm tilt}_{t,x}(\psi'), $$ $$ \nu_{t,x}(dy)= \frac{e^{c\psi(y)}p_{b-t}(y-x)} {\int_{\mathbb R}e^{c\psi(z)}p_{b-t}(z-x)\,dz}\,dy. $$ The tilted density is positive everywhere. Its variance of the nonconstant continuous function $\psi'$ is strictly positive; its mean of $\psi''$ is nonnegative. Thus $v(t,x)>0$ for every $x$, and $\mathbb E v(t,X_t)^4>0$. Combining the limiting inequality with the differentiated identity proves $q'''(t)\ge(1000c^2)^{-1}\mathbb E v(t,X_t)^4>0$. This proves strict convexity of $q'$ on $I$. [OpenAI (2026a), Lemma 2.3][fs-reg]; [Proposition 5.1][fs-curv]. ### 4.6 Why the zero interval remains a separate case When $c=0$, the heat equation gives $q''(t)=\mathbb E\Phi_{xxx}(t,X_t)^2$ without division by $c$. Start the drift-free evolution at an earlier point of $I$; its Gaussian transition kernel makes the law of $X_t$ have a positive density everywhere. If the expectation were zero, continuity would force $\Phi_{xxx}(t,\cdot)\equiv0$. Then $\Phi(t,\cdot)$ would be an even quadratic polynomial. Its one-Lipschitz bound forces that polynomial to be constant, contradicting its bounded distance from $|x|$. Therefore $q''(t)>0$, giving strict increase of $q'$. [OpenAI (2026a), Lemma 2.3][fs-reg]. The analytic certificate is thus a proved input to the gap argument in this source, with the stated model and regularity assumptions. An abstract polynomial or flux lemma assumes those analytic hypotheses; the finite-step comparisons and the transfer argument discharge them. Inspection of the corresponding Lean sources records that construction, while compilation, scoped dependency extraction and Comparator replay remain distinct checks, with their observed outcomes reported in §13.

This is an ordinary source-supported reconstruction, not a new formal replay.
